text:
ana chen: Heads-up — attending MLConf next week. A couple of expense questions before I book: 1) conference registration is on our corporate card, but I'm paying for two team dinners on my personal card (team of 4). 2) The conference lists 2 lunches included. Can I still take a per-diem for the other meals? 3) One dinner will be a pooled split (we paid one check). How should I submit that?

liz (People Ops): Short answers: yes, partially. Submit receipts for anything you want reimbursed, indicate which meals were provided by the conference so we offset per-diem, and for pooled checks include the itemized receipt plus names. More detailed below.

ana chen: thanks! do i need itemized receipts for every coffee/snack too?

liz (People Ops): No need for tiny items under $25 unless you want them counted against your out-of-pocket total. For per-diem, we prefer the per-meal breakdown approach: pick the per-diem option in Expensify (or our Concur form) and then mark which meals the conference covered. If a meal is provided, we deduct that meal's per-diem portion (not the whole day).

ana chen: example please?

liz (People Ops): Example (you can paste into the expense notes):
```
Day 1: breakfast — personal (no), lunch — conference provided (deduct), dinner — personal, dinner amount $220 (split 4 ways)
Day 2: breakfast — hotel (claimed), lunch — personal, dinner — company happy hour (on corporate card)
```
For the split dinner: upload the single itemized restaurant receipt, then create one expense line for the total and add a note listing teammates and the share per person (e.g., "split among Ana C, Marco, Jess, Priya — my share $55"). Finance will reimburse your share.

marco: if credit card was a mix (some items on corporate, some on personal) — do we still mark which items were company paid?

liz (People Ops): Yes — mark company-paid items as "charged to corporate card" in the form. Do NOT submit corporate-card charges for reimbursement. If the vendor only gave one receipt and the corporate card covered part, include both the corporate card transaction (attach statement line) and your personal charge receipt and explain the split in the notes.

josh (Finance): Quick clarifications from finance side: we handle foreign currency conversion at the posted exchange rate on the date of transaction. If you paid tip in local currency, include the math in the notes (amount in local curr -> USD). If you prefer, take a screenshot of the card charge showing the USD amount and attach it. For pooled rideshares: one receipt is fine — include passenger list and the cost per person.

ana chen: what about alcohol? is dinner with client okay?

liz (People Ops): Business meals are reimbursable. Alcohol is reimbursable when appropriate, but keep it reasonable. If the meal is with a client, add the client name/purpose. Avoid excessive charges — finance may flag large alcohol line items.

people-ops-bot: Policy link: https://redwoodintranet.company/travel-policy — travel per-diem, allowable expenses, and required receipts. Use the "Conference meals" section for the standard deduction rules.

ana chen: last one — do i need preapproval for dinner over $200?

josh (Finance): If a single meal (post-tip) per person > $200, please get manager approval and add it to the expense note. If the total check is high because of the group size but your share is reasonable, include the per-person breakout and manager sign-off if possible.

liz (People Ops): If you want, drop the draft expense here and we can sanity-check before you submit. :thumbsup:

ana chen: awesome, i'll post the receipt bundle here after the trip. thanks all!
